source_or_reason: Two-way circulation beyond WPP net migration, fraction of population per year, scaled by each country's mobility. step7_validate.py (foreign_born_check) starts from the UN 1990 foreign-born stocks and simulates 1990-2020: the UN 2020 world total (252 million in the modelled countries) is matched at about 0.0001, the population-weighted country error is lowest at 0.0002 and the country-mean error at 0.0003; above 0.0004 every error grows (0.0011, the old central value, gives 407 million). Gross flow estimates (Abel & Cohen, about 0.0016 per year) are higher because many movers return: the model counts a returning emigrant as foreign-born in their own country, so it needs the lower, stock-consistent rate. Gross churn is therefore understated; foreign-born stocks are not.

How strictly the flow solver enforces WPP's net migration against the observed migrant network: flows F = a K b with a = (E / K b)^rho and b = (I / K' a)^rho. rho = 1 enforces both WPP margins exactly; WPP's projected margins are partly inconsistent with the network (for example Pakistan keeps emigrating about 0.5-1 million a year while Gulf net immigration falls to almost zero after 2030), which then forces emigrants into whichever countries have positive net immigration (Pakistan would supply 46% of UK immigrants in 2020-2050 against 8% of its 2020 foreign-born). Lower rho lets both margins give way. The 1990-2020 corridor test in step7_validate.py (migration_corridor_check.csv) fits destinations' origin mixes best near 0.75; the range spans that uncertainty.
